categories.name: Anthropology
categories.description: Anthropology programs covering cultural, biological, and linguistic anthropology and archaeology — the comparative study of human societies past and present.

tips.title: Volunteer at a museum or heritage site
tips.detail: Regular shifts at a museum, historic site, or cultural centre — helping with collections, interpretation, or public programming — show sustained interest in human cultures and material history.

tips.title: Look for archaeology field schools and public digs
tips.detail: Many universities, museums, and local archaeological societies run summer field schools or community dig days open to high-school students. Even a single season of survey or lab work is a standout application story.

tips.title: Learn a second language
tips.detail: Sustained language study, whether at school or through community classes, signals seriousness about fieldwork and cross-cultural research — the core of anthropological work.

programs.name: Anthropology
programs.notes: Admission is to the Faculty of Arts & Science; the anthropology major is declared after first year. Both BA streams (sociocultural, linguistic) and a BSc stream (evolutionary anthropology) are offered.

tips.title: OUAC application deadline
tips.detail: Apply through OUAC by January 15, 2027 — the equal-consideration date for Fall 2027 entry to Ontario universities.

tips.title: President's/entrance scholar consideration
tips.detail: Admitted students with averages of roughly 92% and above are automatically considered for University of Toronto entrance scholarships, including President's Scholars awards.

tips.title: Application deadline

tips.detail: All admitted students are automatically considered for McGill's one-time Basic Entrance Scholarship. Recent recipients have typically presented averages of roughly 93% and above; exact cutoffs vary by year and faculty.

programs.name: Anthropology
programs.notes: UBC admission is broad-based: grades plus the Personal Profile. Entry is through the Faculty of Arts; the anthropology major is declared after first year. BC equivalents of the listed courses are English Studies 12 and a Grade 12 math.

supplementary.name: Personal Profile
supplementary.description: Short written responses about experiences, activities, and what you learned from them; weighted alongside grades for all direct-entry UBC applicants.

tips.title: Take the Personal Profile seriously
tips.detail: The Personal Profile is weighted alongside your marks. Museum and heritage volunteering, field-school experience, and language study make strong, specific answers for anthropology applicants.

tips.title: UBC application deadline
tips.detail: Apply through EducationPlannerBC by January 15, 2027 for September 2027 entry. Verify the current cycle's dates on UBC's admissions site before relying on them.

tips.title: Major entrance awards are profile-based
tips.detail: UBC's major entrance awards, including Presidential Scholars Awards, are selected from the application and Personal Profile rather than an automatic average cutoff; some require a separate application.

programs.name: Anthropology
programs.notes: Memorial also has a separate, internationally known Department of Archaeology; students interested in digs and material culture can combine the two or switch between them. tips.title: Rolling admission — apply by early spring
tips.detail: Memorial reviews applications on a rolling basis rather than against a single equal-consideration date. Applying by early spring — ideally before March — is advised for the best access to program seats, residence, and entrance award consideration.
